title: Utility Order for Washington-St. Tammany Electric Cooperative, Inc., ex parte. — Order No. S-37945 accepts the Staff Report and Recommendation filed into the record on September 11, 2026, and the Commission expresses its non-opposition to Washington-St. Tammany Electric Cooperative, Inc request to September 11, 2026, subject to the conditions detailed within. This matter was considered at the October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session.

documents.text:
LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                    ORDER NUMBER S-37945

   WASHINGTON-ST. TAMMANY ELECTRIC COOPERATIVE, INC., EX PARTE.

Docket No. S-37945, In re: Request for Letter of Non-Opposition to secure a loan for WST's
construction work plan, including mortgaging assets related thereto.

                 (Decided at the October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


                                               ORDER

    I.       Overview
          On June 1, 2026, Washington-St. Tammany Electric Cooperative Inc. (“WST” or the
“Cooperative”) filed the above captioned request (the “Request”) pursuant to Louisiana Public Service
Commission (“LPSC” or the “Commission”) General Order dated March 18, 1994 (the “March 1994
General Order”). The Request sought the Commission’s authorization for WST to enter into a loan
agreement with the United States Department of Agriculture Rural Utilities Service (“RUS”) wherein
WST will grant a conventional mortgage for a proposed $108,230,353 Construction Work Plan.
WST’s Request asserted that the proceeds from the loan would permit WST to implement necessary
system improvements that are designed to improve reliability, maintain adequate voltage levels,
address aging infrastructure, support projected growth, and maintain a safe and reliable electric service
throughout the Cooperatives service territory. The Request was published in the Commission’s
Official Bulletin #1377 dated June 05, 2026 for fifteen (15) day intervention period. No interventions
were received during, or subsequent to, the intervention period.


    II.      Jurisdiction and Applicable Law
          The Commission exercises regulatory jurisdiction over all utility companies, including
WST, pursuant to Article 4, Section 21, of the Louisiana Constitution and applicable Commission
Orders adopted pursuant to that authority.

    La Const. Art. IV, Sec. 21 provides in pertinent part:

                 The Commission shall regulate all common carriers and public utilities and
                 have such other regulatory authority as provided by law. It shall adopt and
                 enforce reasonable rules, regulations, and procedures necessary for the
                 discharge of its duties, and perform other duties provided by law.

    General Order dated November 13, 1996:

                 Approval of this transaction is specifically required pursuant to the
                 Commission’s General Order dated November 13, 1996. In particular, the
                 General Order states Item Number 1,
                 No public utility shall issue any security or assume any obligation or
                 liability as guarantor, endorser, surety, or otherwise in respect of any
                 security of any other public utility, or of any other person, until it has been
                 authorized to do so by Order of this Commission.

    Further under Item Number 5 of the same Order:



                                                                                   Order No. S-37945
                                                                                              Page 1
                   This General Order does not modify in any manner the General Order issued
                  by this Commission dated 3/18/94 related to Commission approval of sales,
                  leases, etc. Any security issuance that requires a utility to “sell, assign, lease,
                  transfer, mortgage, or otherwise dispose of or encumber” the property or
                  assets of the utility must be approved by the Commission under the
                  standards set forth in the 3/18/94 General Order as well.

    General Order dated March 18, 1994:

           Approval of this transaction is specifically required pursuant to the Commission’s
General Order dated March 18, 1994 as the loan terms require a pledge of assets of the
Company to secure the RUS funds.


    III.          WST’s Request
           WST sought approval of its 2025-2028 Construction Work Plan (“CWP”). WST asserted that
the system improvements included are necessary to provide service for its 58,769 consumers at an
average monthly consumption of 1,745 kWh per consumer. WST has indicated that the present system
peak demands total 279,252 kW, and typically occurs during the winter months. WST’s projected
system peak is estimated to be at 345,470 kW. In order to meet this projected system peak as well as
address reliability and system energy losses, WST proposed a construction plan that includes categories
for total system improvements, consumer additions, and transmission services. The work plan
consisted of a four (4) year plan where approximately $42,165,391 would be spent in the first year,
$21,165,770 would be spent in the second year, $21,199,292 would be spent in the third year, and
$23,699,891 would be spent in the fourth year. The CWP outlined work that is needed to support the
projected peak demand, increase reliability, and lower system energy losses and help reduce power
costs to customers moving forward. WST has identified it will utilize short term lending from current
lenders at market interest rates to start construction of the included projects prior to paying those off
once project completion occurs.
           WST is seeking to enter into a loan agreement valued at approximately $108,230,353 with
RUS, with interest expenses determined at the time of each loan advance. The loan will be disbursed
over the course of four years as the construction work plan progresses. The total funds will not be
drawn in one lump sum, but will be drawn to reimburse capital construction projects upon completion
as outlined in the construction work plan. Pursuant to the Loan Documents, advances may be made
through September 29, 2031. The associated Treasury Direct Note has a final maturity date of June 1,
2061.
           In support of the Cooperative’s request, WST submitted an eighteen (18) point analysis
pursuant to the March 1994 General Order, a construction work plan, loan documents, responses to
data requests that sought additional financial information including financial results, debt service
obligations, and the impact of the proposed construction work plan in terms of plant additions, interest
and principal costs, and depreciation changes for WST. Additionally, WST provided Staff with a copy
of letters from RUS whereas, Mr. Deismon Ross, General Field Representative and Mr. Karl
Elmshaeuser, Administrator, indicated approval of the CWP and associated loan was granted.


    IV.           Staff Review and Recommendation
           Staff conducted a thorough review of WST’s application and all supporting documentation as
                                                                                       Order No. S-37945
                                                                                                  Page 2
 referenced above. The terms and conditions of the financing agreement require WST to grant a
conventional mortgage of the Cooperative’s utility assets. WST is required by its lenders to maintain a
specific range of certain leverage ratios. Leverage ratios are generally used to assess a Cooperative’s
ability to meet financial obligations.
        Staff sought additional information in regard to financials to determine what WST’s current and
historical coverage ratios are and have been over the previous three years. Staff’s review indicated that
WST has met or exceeded the leverage ratios required of its lenders for the vast majority of the period
from 2021 to 2025. Although WST may have been slightly under once of the metrics in a particular
single year, WST’s lenders required a best two of three average to exceed the previously mentioned
requirements and WST’s Formula Rate Plan is designed to allow WST to maintain these ratios with a
reasonable cushion to ensure that the Cooperative is financially stable.
        Based upon the information provided, it appeared that RUS is willing and able to provide WST
the total proceeds requested of the approximate $108 million to cover the projects listed in the
Construction Work Plan. Additionally, the metrics showed that the short-term lenders of CoBank and
CFC’s metrics are also being met which show favorable means for WST to ensure it has access to both
short-term and long-term debt needed for these projects.
        Staff found that the current Formula Rate Plan design is favorable for WST as it allows the
Cooperative to adjust rates based on a bandwidth utilizing a TIER of a 1.40 to a 1.60 where the TIER
requirement of its lenders is a 1.25. Additionally, WST’s current FRP contains secondary revenue checks
to ensure that OTIER is a minimum of a 1.20 where the requirement is a 1.10 from the lenders and MDSC
is a 1.40 where the requirement is a 1.25 from the lenders. This ensures that WST is able to adjust its
rates per annum which makes is significantly more likely that they are able to hit the best two of three-
year averages for these metrics. Keeping at the requirement or above the requirement of the coverage
ratios for its lenders ensures that WST has continued access to capital for its operations. WST indicated
in response to data requests that it is currently reviewing its rates and plan on filing a new rate case in the
near future where these new loans and operating expenses would be acknowledged to ensure financial
stability moving forward.
        The RUS loan will be secured by a mortgage on WST’s utility assets. Therefore, the transaction
is subject to the March 18, 1994 General Order. Staff reviewed WST’s responses to the 18-point analysis.
The Cooperative has stated there will not be a transfer of assets and that the transaction in in the best
interest of its members based on the following:

                The mortgage will in no way interfere with WST’s provision of safe, reliable, and
                 adequate service to its members and instead would provide access to capital that is critical
                 to WST’s efforts to complete its Construction Work Plan to effectively provide that
                 service.
                The Construction Work Plan completion and associated mortgage would create a more
                 resilient and reliable electric service for WST and the members it serves and create both
                 short term benefits and long-term benefits in terms of that reliability.
                The proposed transaction would be a stimulus to the local and state economies in terms
                 of purchase of materials and labor but also in terms of growth of residential consumers
                 that WST is projecting in its service territory.

                                                                                        Order No. S-37945
                                                                                                   Page 3
                  WST has the ability to obtain all necessary health, safety, and other permits as requested
                  and has a history of compliance with the Commission and other regulatory agencies.
                 WST doesn’t believe there should be any additional conditions on the proposed
                  transaction.
        In summary, WST provided Staff with an in-depth look at the financials as well as projects built
into the Construction Work Plan. WST was able to meet the necessary financial metrics required for the
loan process by the lenders and the Cooperative is currently operating under a Formula Rate Plan that
would help to ensure future financial metrics are met at a minimum.

        After the extensive review, Staff concurred that the transaction is in the public interest and
will have no immediate effect on rates or terms of service for WST members. Staff recommended
that the Commission expresses its non-opposition to the Request subject to the following
conditions:

   1. The Cooperative file into the record of this proceeding a copy of the signed loan agreement,
        outlining the final terms and conditions, within thirty (30) days of the loan closing date.
   2. Should the loan agreement be modified in any way, prior to issuance of funds, the newly
        revised agreement shall be filed into the record of this proceeding no later than fifteen (15)
        days after such modification.
   3. If the signed loan documents have not been filed within ninety (90) days of an Order in
        this proceeding, the Cooperative, must file a status update into the record on or before
        ninety (90) days from the date of an Order. The Commission reserves the right to rescind
        its non-opposition if the loan documents are not filed within ninety (90) days of the date of
        an Order in this proceeding.
   4. The Cooperative shall file a report twice yearly to update the status of the four-year
        Construction Work Plan and include the total amount budgeted from the original filing,
        the total amount spent, the remaining totals for work to be done, and a timeline for
        completion of that work. Additionally, the Cooperative shall include the status of any short
        term debt totals and accounts utilized for construction purposes as well as the status of any
        draws from the original amounts that have been taken and alleviated that short term debt.
   5. This non-opposition is granted without prejudice to the authority of the Commission to
        make investigations and require any reasonably necessary change that the Commission
        may legally find to be in the public interest.
   6. This Order will be effective immediately upon issuance by the Commission.

   V.             Commission Consideration
        This matter was considered at the Commission’s October 22, 2026 Business and Executive
Session. On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Vice Chairman Coussan, and
unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to accept the Staff Report and Recommendation filed
into the record on September 11, 2026.
THEREFORE, IT IS ORDERED:

        That the Louisiana Public Service Commission expresses its non-opposition to the


                                                                                      Order No. S-37945
                                                                                                 Page 4
 Company’s Request and Credit Facilities, subject to the following conditions:


   1. The Cooperative file into the record of this proceeding a copy of the signed loan agreement,
       outlining the final terms and conditions, within thirty (30) days of the loan closing date.
   2. Should the loan agreement be modified in any way, prior to issuance of funds, the newly
       revised agreement shall be filed into the record of this proceeding no later than fifteen (15)
       days after such modification.
   3. If the signed loan documents have not been filed within ninety (90) days of an Order in
       this proceeding, the Cooperative, must file a status update into the record on or before
       ninety (90) days from the date of an Order. The Commission reserves the right to rescind
       its non-opposition if the loan documents are not filed within ninety (90) days of the date of
       an Order in this proceeding.
   4. The Cooperative shall file a report twice yearly to update the status of the four-year
       Construction Work Plan and include the total amount budgeted from the original filing,
       the total amount spent, the remaining totals for work to be done, and a timeline for
       completion of that work. Additionally, the Cooperative shall include the status of any short
       term debt totals and accounts utilized for construction purposes as well as the status of any
       draws from the original amounts that have been taken and alleviated that short term debt.
   5. This non-opposition is granted without prejudice to the authority of the Commission to
       make investigations and require any reasonably necessary change that the Commission
       may legally find to be in the public interest.
   6. This Order will be effective immediately upon issuance by the Commission.
This Order is effective immediately.


BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA
November 20, 2026
